title: Segmented Angular Pre-Processing for Accurate and Efficient In-Memory Vector Similarity Search
problem: Energy-efficient vector similarity search (VSS) using cosine similarity in high-dimensional spaces, particularly for few-shot learning and approximate nearest neighbor search, while reducing vector data movement.
motivation: VSS incurs substantial energy and computational overhead due to frequent vector transfers and complex cosine similarity calculations; prior TCAM-based methods focus on spatial metrics (L∞, L₁) but exhibit poor approximation of angular metrics like cosine similarity.
method: Seg-Cos framework leverages both EX-TCAM and Best-TCAM for angular VSS via dedicated preprocessing and encoding: vectors are segmented and encoded as circular ranges based on angles and magnitudes; Locality-aware Compute Mapping (LCM) reduces row activations; LUT Aggregation (LAG) enables multi-precision computations by combining multiple small LUT results.
key_novelty: First TCAM-based framework directly approximating cosine similarity (angular metric) within TCAM, compatible with both EX-TCAM and Best-TCAM architectures.
contributions: Seg-Cos framework for direct angular VSS in TCAM (first such framework)
Segmented vector encoding as circular ranges for angle-magnitude representation
Locality-aware Compute Mapping to minimize row activations

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 1.41x energy efficiency improvement in FSL; 2x energy efficiency in ANNS
metrics.accuracy: 2.2% higher accuracy in FSL over EX-TCAM methods; 10-52% recall rate improvement in ANNS

primary_theme: Angular vector similarity search via TCAM preprocessing and in-memory encoding
